question: Elder general#12825: is the budget 2q term (0.0137) understated ~12x, per the -3.44pp/weight slope? Reading (a) slope overstated -> n flat; reading (b) depolarizing model understates depth -> n reopens.
method: fit accept-vs-A-weight per arm on the PAIRED bake-off (same A-set in all three arms, one epoch, n=96 each)
paired_structural_result: Toffoli arm -0.45 vs redesign arm -0.50, difference 0.05 pp/weight — the redesign did NOT change the weight sensitivity, exactly as Elder predicted structurally (A-planting is STATE PREP, untouched). His structural reasoning is CONFIRMED; the magnitude is what turns out to be small.
verdict: READING (a) FAVOURED: the pooled bake-off excludes the -3.44 point estimate, and the N1 slope was never significant. So the budget 2q term is not badly understated and n stays flat — PROVISIONALLY.
caveats: individual arms are underpowered (n=96) and exclude neither value
the two datasets OVERLAP (both admit ~-2), so they are not formally inconsistent — the bake-off merely excludes the N1 POINT
the bake-off is ONE epoch; if the slope is epoch-dependent neither dataset can see it
survey Output 2 remains the definitive test: 500-800 rows ACROSS EPOCHS, which is the only design here that controls epoch-dependence of the slope itself
position: readout-limited is ESTABLISHED (budget closes on a MEASURED 3.4x inflation); n-is-flat is FAVOURED but PROVISIONAL, and I am not writing it into the design brief as settled — Elder is right that a conclusion inheriting a known-suspect model deserves the softer label.
